headline: AI models forecast cellular responses to perturbations in silico
label: Ai Virtual Cell Perturbation Models
summary: Virtual cell models are moving from architecture proposals toward benchmarks and trustworthiness criteria for unmeasured cellular responses.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predictive modeling of cellular perturbation responses, in which learned representations stand in for experiments not yet performed. Architectures vary: a transformer delta-expression encoder classifies psilocybin-induced differential expression from snRNA-seq pseudobulk (69.4% accuracy on 623 examples), MRFlow casts perturbation response as conditional flow-matching transport between control and perturbed latent distributions, and scDEFT treats drugs as conditioning operators on single-cell latents. ProteinTalks extends the virtual cell concept to time-resolved proteomics. A 13-method benchmark across 25 datasets assesses unseen-gene prediction, and a roadmap defines evidential requirements for trustworthy virtual cells. What is new relative to signature discovery is the explicit framing of perturbation prediction as an evaluable, experimentally grounded task, though several item summaries describe computational benchmarks rather than prospective experimental validation.
